preamble: The GOAT diphthong [oʊ] reduces to schwa [ə] in unstressed syllables in English. In stress alternations the same root shows a full diphthong when stressed and schwa when unstressed (photograph [ˈfoʊtəɡræf] vs photography [fəˈtɒɡrəfi]). In many nonstandard varieties, final unstressed -ow is reduced to schwa and merges with the -er/-ar ending, as eye-dialect spellings such as feller 'fellow' and winder 'window' show. Careful standard speech often keeps a reduced rounded vowel [ɵ] in words like willow instead.

examples.note: Stress-conditioned reduction: the first o is the GOAT diphthong under stress and schwa when unstressed.
Reduction of final unstressed -ow to schwa and conflation with -er; attested in written dialect from the 19th century (Stephen Crane, 1899).
The same final -ow reduction; a pronunciation spelling attested since at least 1868.
